what_it_does: Designing a modern computer chip is enormously complex — it involves writing millions of lines of hardware description code, verifying correctness, optimizing for power and speed, and placing and routing billions of transistors. This position or review paper argues that large language models (LLMs — AI systems trained on vast amounts of text and code that can understand and generate language) are becoming a driving force in automating these design tasks. It surveys where LLMs are already being applied in the chip design workflow, assesses how ready they are for different categories of tasks, and proposes directions for future research. The paper does not present new experimental results; instead it maps out the opportunity space and the open problems that remain before AI can reliably assist or automate significant portions of chip design.
